newsitem.title: FRANCE: French punish guerrilla Carlos "wildebeest" crack.
newsitem.headline: French punish guerrilla Carlos "wildebeest" crack.

text.p: French prison authorities have disciplined guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal" for calling a prison guard a "wildebeest", justice sources said on Friday.

Carlos, held in a Paris prison while awaiting trial for a series of bomb attacks in France in the 1980s, was given a suspended 10 days in solitary confinement after calling a guard, "You wildebeest, you!".
His lawyer has written a letter of protest to the prison director maintaining that a wildebeest was merely the name of an animal and not an insult, the sources said.

Justice authorities meanwhile dropped plans to call Carlos in for questioning on Friday by France's top anti-terrorist investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere over the Paris killings of two French secret agents and their Lebanese informer in 1975.

The three men and a counter-intelligence chief, all unarmed, had called at a Left Bank flat in Paris. The man who opened the door shot them after a brief discussion and fled. Only the counter-intelligence chief survived.
Carlos, whose real name is Illich Ramirez Sanchez, was found guilty of the killings and sentenced in absentia in 1992 to life in jail.
Under French law he is entitled to a retrial since he did not attend the hearings.
Carlos, in French prison since 1994, disputes experts' reports that his fingerprints were found at the Paris flat and that the type of pistol used indicates he was the killer, the sources said.

French police accuse Carlos of killing 83 people in a series of attacks in Europe and the Middle East. The boldest attack with which he was linked was the kidnapping of 11 OPEC oil ministers in Vienna in 1975.
